title: Interactive SLO matrix with error-budget depletion mitigation and staged rollback criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: PRD: Define a compact, actionable SLO matrix and a deterministic rollout gating policy for interactive/response-generation routes (chat and single-turn text generation). This ticket consolidates requirements, clarifies scope changes from the last SLA discussion, and captures acceptance criteria so engineering and SRE can implement guards, alerts, and automation. Scope: hosted API and Dedicated configurations for interactive endpoints. Out of scope: embeddings only endpoints and on-prem private packaging (will be covered in follow-up). Goal: ensure we can ship a reproducible canary -> staged rollout flow that automatically halts or rolls back when error budget burn or latency regressions exceed thresholds, with explicit acceptance criteria and runbooks for manual override.
acceptance_criteria: Define SLO matrix covering p50/p95/p99 latency and availability for route classes: interactive-chat, short-completion (<256 tokens), long-completion (>=256 tokens).

SLO values are documented and agreed: interactive-chat p50 <= 60ms, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 520ms; short-completion p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 900ms; availability >= 99.95% per region for Hosted Standard tier.

Error budget policy: per-release error budget is 1% monthly for interactive-chat; automated canary rollback triggers when rolling 5% of traffic for 30 minutes and observed burn rate exceeds 3x baseline or absolute error rate > 0.5% for the canary traffic window.
Canary gating automated checks implemented in runtime CI: latency regressions measured against baseline using the same traffic profile and traffic-weighted shadowing where possible.
Define and publish monitoring queries and dashboard (Datadog/Grafana) links for SLOs and canary alerts; dashboards show rolling 1h/6h/24h windows and burn-rate metric.
Runbook created and linked that describes manual escalation steps, rollback commands, and how to initiate a temporary degraded-mode (lower-cost model variant) if rollback is not possible.
QA: end-to-end test that simulates a canary rollout and triggers both pass and fail conditions; test results recorded in PR and linked to this ticket.
Operational owners (SRE/Runtime/PM) sign-off in comments and approve the final SLO matrix and rollout gates before release cut.
SLOs published in customer-facing operational contract doc and included in Console per-route SLO display where applicable.
decisions: Use percentile-based latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) rather than average latencies to avoid masking tail regressions.
Adopt a two-tier error-budget policy: a conservative public-facing SLA (availability) and a tighter internal SLO for per-route latency to guide rollouts.
Automated canary evaluation will be performed at 5% -> 20% -> 50% ramp with mandatory 30m observation windows at each step unless approval is granted to skip by SRE after manual review.

Fallback model variant (quantized, lower-memory variant) will be the first graceful-degradation path for performance-induced regressions; switching to a lower-quality model requires explicit PM approval and customer impact notes.
Regional SLO deviations allowed up to +/-0.05% availability during short-term cloud provider incidents; permanent differences require an explicit regional SLO document.
tradeoffs: Tighter latency SLOs reduce acceptable batching and may increase cost; we accept higher cost for interactive-chat routes during peak PLG flows and optimize later with batching heuristics.

Automated rollbacks minimize blast radius but increase risk of unnecessary rollbacks on noisy signals; mitigate by combining absolute error thresholds with burn-rate checks and min-sample-size guards.
Using the quantized fallback model reduces cost but can introduce prompt-dependent quality regressions; we'll track quality regressions in Redwood Optimize evaluations.
monitoring_queries: prometheus:burn_rate = (errors_last_1h / errors_last_30d_expected) - burn rate heuristic for alerts
grafana:rolling_window(p99, 1h) for long-completion routes for tail visibility
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - Preflight: unit/integ tests passing, model artifact checksum validated, baseline perf profile exists.
Gate 1 - Canary 5% for 30m: require no regression > 10% in p95 vs baseline AND canary_error_rate < 0.5% AND burn_rate < 3x.
Gate 2 - 20% for 30m: require stability vs baseline: p99 drift < 20% and cumulative error_budget_usage < 10% for the release window.
Gate 3 - 50% for 60m: manual SRE sign-off if any threshold near limits; otherwise auto-ramp to 100%.
Abort condition: any single measurement where absolute availability drops > 1% or canary error rate > 1.5% triggers automatic rollback to previous model variant and page to on-call.
error_budget_policy: Monthly error budget per route: interactive-chat 1% (hard), short-completion 2%, long-completion 3%. If cumulative burn over 7 days exceeds 50% of monthly budget, block non-critical rollouts and require mitigation plan. Critical security fixes are exempted but require retrospective post-deploy.
